Making BART safer in earthquakes

Full-scale testing at the PEER Center

How much shaking should trigger trains to slow down or stop?

UC Berkeley researchers combine analytical studies and large-scale experiments to help evaluate BART earthquake early warning thresholds—supporting passenger safety while reducing unnecessary interruptions to transit service.

Three complementary experimental studies
01
Ballasted tracksInvestigating ballast disturbance
02
Aerial structuresInvestigating damage relevant to train passage
03
Full-scale railcarsInvestigating train uplift during earthquake shaking

Together with numerical modeling and uncertainty analysis, these tests inform recommendations for future shaking thresholds.
